title: Smart PAW – Smart Pet Feeder
shortDescription: An ESP32 feeder with weight-based dispensing, RFID identification, and jam recovery.
description: An automated pet-feeding system using an ESP32, weight measurement, RFID-based identification, and servo-controlled dispensing.
overview: Smart PAW combines embedded control, sensing, identity, and mechanical actuation into an automated feeding workflow.
objectives: Monitor feeding progress and recover from jams
implementation: Load-cell readings are used to track dispensing progress.
RFID, LCD, keypad, and servo peripherals form the user interaction loop.
A six-step recovery sequence handles a detected jam.
contribution: This was a group project; individual contributions should be documented alongside the relevant hardware or firmware work when confirmed.
futureImprovements: Improve enclosure and feeding mechanism validation

title: Dino Runner With Neural Network
shortDescription: A Pygame Dino Runner agent trained with a Deep Q-Learning style workflow.
description: A game-playing reinforcement learning agent with replay memory, a target network, and exploration scheduling.
overview: The project explores how an agent can learn game actions from state features and reward feedback.
implementation: Experience replay stores transitions for mini-batch learning.
Epsilon-greedy exploration balances discovery and exploitation.
A target network and Double-DQN-style target calculation reduce learning instability.

title: Student Authentication and Attendance Management System
shortDescription: A multi-service authentication and attendance platform with a React dashboard.
description: A service-oriented system with separate FastAPI services and PostgreSQL databases for student workflows.
overview: The system separates authentication and attendance concerns while providing a dashboard prototype for users and administrators.
objectives: Create a maintainable local development workflow
implementation: Three FastAPI services use separate PostgreSQL databases.
JWT and bcrypt support authenticated role-based flows.
Docker and GitHub Actions support repeatable development and checks.

title: Friday AI Agent
shortDescription: A local-LLM assistant with semantic memory and practical desktop automation tools.
description: A personal AI assistant designed around locally hosted language models and automation capabilities.
overview: Friday experiments with privacy-conscious local inference, tool use, semantic memory, and desktop workflows.
objectives: Connect a local model to useful tools
Keep automation capabilities explicit and inspectable
implementation: FastAPI exposes the assistant backend.
Ollama provides local LLM integration and ChromaDB provides semantic memory.
Implemented tools include search, application launching, file management, notifications, and IMAP email summaries.
futureImprovements: Document which automation flows remain experimental

title: Rubik Cube Solver
shortDescription: Computer vision, cube-state interpretation, Kociemba solving, and 3D visualization.
description: A solver combining camera-based scanning, color classification, a Flask API, and optional servo integration.
overview: The project turns camera observations into a cube representation, computes a solution, and visualizes the sequence.
objectives: Produce and visualize a valid solving sequence
implementation: HSV-based classification supports camera scanning.
The Kociemba two-phase algorithm computes solutions.
Three.js renders the cube while Flask and optional ESP32/PCA9685 components connect the workflow.

title: Supermarket Chatbot with NLP
shortDescription: An NLP assistant that locates products and shelf positions from natural-language queries.
description: A full-stack supermarket assistant using preprocessing, lemmatization, and fuzzy matching.
overview: Users can ask for products naturally and receive inventory and shelf-location responses.
implementation: Text is normalized and lemmatized before matching.
A JSON inventory powers product and shelf lookup.
FastAPI, React, Docker, and CI form the application workflow.

title: YOLO Custom Bottle and Cup Detector
shortDescription: A small object-detection experiment covering dataset preparation, training, and evaluation.
description: A custom YOLO learning project for detecting bottles and cups.
overview: This project is a focused learning experiment rather than a production-grade detector.
implementation: The dataset contains two classes: bottle and cup.
Training uses a 80/10/10 split and 30 epochs.

title: Distributed Chat Application
shortDescription: A phased real-time chat system evolving from a core backend to reliable distributed services.
description: A distributed real-time chat application built around asynchronous services, persistence, multi-instance communication, and resilient client-server communication.
overview: This is the current flagship systems project. Its timeline makes the boundary between implemented reliability mechanisms and future work explicit.
problem: A single real-time server is difficult to scale and recover reliably when connections, events, or dependencies fail.
objectives: Process events reliably with idempotent consumers
Improve resilience without claiming exactly-once delivery
architecture: Phases 1–3 combine FastAPI, PostgreSQL, WebSockets, Nginx, Redis Pub/Sub, and RabbitMQ. Phase 4 adds reliability and security work incrementally; Kubernetes remains a future deployment goal.
implementation: Redis Pub/Sub allows backend instances to exchange real-time events.
RabbitMQ integration includes ACK/NACK, retries, dead-letter queues, stable UUIDs, idempotency, and a transactional outbox.
Server-side encryption is implemented; client-side one-to-one encryption is a Phase 4 objective.
contribution: The case study separates verified implementation from ongoing Phase 4 work so that planned resilience features are not presented as complete.

developmentPhases.name: Phase 1 – Core Backend and Real-Time Communication
developmentPhases.description: FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL persistence, JWT authentication, and WebSocket communication.

developmentPhases.name: Phase 2 – Distributed Communication
developmentPhases.description: Multiple backend instances, Nginx, Redis Pub/Sub, and cross-instance events.

developmentPhases.name: Phase 3 – Reliable Messaging and Event Processing
developmentPhases.description: RabbitMQ, ACK/NACK, retries, DLQs, idempotency, stable UUIDs, outbox, and server-side encryption.

developmentPhases.name: Phase 4 – Reliability, Resilience and Security
developmentPhases.description: Presence TTLs, heartbeats, reconnect, missed-message sync, graceful shutdown, health/readiness, and client-side encryption objectives.

developmentPhases.name: Planned – Kubernetes Deployment
developmentPhases.description: Future container orchestration, service discovery, probes, scaling, and recovery experiments. No manifests or cluster deployment are claimed.

futureImprovements: Explore a Kubernetes/K3s deployment after application development

title: BruteForceAttack
shortDescription: An educational substitution-cipher implementation with basic cryptanalysis.
description: A C++17 learning project supporting encryption, decryption, frequency analysis, and key enumeration.
overview: The project demonstrates classical cipher mechanics and should not be treated as a production security tool.
implementation: Supports substitution encryption and decryption.
Uses frequency analysis and known-plaintext assistance.
Enumerates five-character keys across 120 permutations.

title: MediaPipe Computer Vision Projects
shortDescription: A collection of real-time landmark and interaction experiments with OpenCV.
description: A set of computer vision experiments using MediaPipe landmarks and OpenCV.
overview: The repository explores how landmarks can support interactive visual applications.
implementation: Experiments include hand and face landmarks, gesture classification, rock-paper-scissors, drowsiness-related work, smile detection, two-hand interaction, and image capture.

title: Library Management System
shortDescription: A Java Swing desktop application for books, users, borrowing, and returns.
description: A desktop library management application with due-date handling and overdue-loan restrictions.
overview: The application models common library workflows while connecting a Java desktop interface to PostgreSQL persistence.
implementation: Supports book and user management.
Handles borrowing, returns, due dates, and overdue-loan restrictions.

title: CertificateAuthenticator
shortDescription: A certificate verification platform combining Spring Boot authentication with blockchain verification.
description: A certificate authentication platform with database persistence, protected downloads, and Ethereum Sepolia integration.
overview: The project explores how a conventional authenticated backend can connect certificate records to blockchain-based verification.
implementation: Supports certificate upload and verification.
JWT and BCrypt protect authenticated workflows and password-protected downloads.
Web3j connects the backend to Ethereum Sepolia and a Solidity smart contract.

title: MealBridge
shortDescription: A food donation platform connecting donors and recipients with a Spring Boot backend.
description: A group food redistribution platform with geospatial data, real-time communication, and a prediction service.
overview: MealBridge combines a secure Java backend with geospatial persistence, live updates, and a quantity prediction service.
contribution: My primary contribution was the Spring Boot backend and DevOps part. The platform-level features are described as group work.
implementation: Spring Security and JWT protect backend workflows.
PostgreSQL/PostGIS supports location-aware data.
WebSocket/STOMP and a Flask Random Forest service extend the backend.

title: Tetris
shortDescription: A Java Swing desktop game with local two-player play and PostgreSQL leaderboards.
description: A desktop Tetris implementation with a 20×10 board, seven tetromino types, and configurable levels.
overview: This project focuses on game-state management, desktop UI, local multiplayer, and persistence.
implementation: Implements local two-player gameplay.
Stores leaderboard data in PostgreSQL.
Supports 35 configured levels and seven tetromino types.

title: UR5e ROS 2 Gazebo Simulation
shortDescription: A simulated UR5e robotic arm controlled through ROS 2 and Gazebo.
description: A robotics simulation project using ROS 2 Jazzy, Gazebo Harmonic, and joint trajectory control.
overview: The project develops control workflows in simulation; it does not claim physical robot testing.
implementation: The ur5e_python_control package exposes move_ur5e.
Joint trajectories use /scaled_joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory.
The simulation launches through ur_simulation_gz.

title: N-Queens Simulation
shortDescription: A modular backtracking solver and visualization-oriented implementation of N-Queens.
description: A Python implementation that explores valid queen placements while rejecting conflicts.
overview: The solver models the N-Queens constraints and uses backtracking to explore a board without sharing rows, columns, or diagonals.
objectives: Test the algorithm independently of visualization
implementation: A base solver abstraction supports algorithm implementations.
The backtracking solver places a queen, checks constraints, and backtracks when a branch is invalid.
Utility and board modules support visualization and tests.

title: Adaptive CPU-GPU Scheduler
shortDescription: An academic HPC project for adaptive scheduling in a video enhancement pipeline.
description: A two-semester, 5-credit project exploring CPU-only, GPU-only, and hybrid scheduling on one machine.
overview: The pipeline covers decode, resize, Gaussian blur, CLAHE, Sobel edge detection, sharpening, and encode.
problem: Choosing CPU/GPU resources and overlap settings is workload-dependent, so static scheduling may leave compute or transfer capacity unused.
objectives: Tune streams, buffers, queues, and frames in flight
Use feedback to adapt CPU-GPU allocation
implementation: Hybrid execution processes different frames on CPU and GPU simultaneously.
The feedback equation is E_new = alpha * T_actual + (1 - alpha) * T_old.
Planned baselines include sequential, threaded, pinned CPU modes and CUDA stream counts of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16.
futureImprovements: Report measured throughput, utilization, transfer, kernel, and queue metrics
